contract.review_scope: Body-level static contract; transitive application and called-module completeness are separate.
contract.purpose: Build work-group chart plus monitor summary counts.
inputs_defaults: filterCriteria nvarchar(MAX), culture nvarchar(10); no defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: Absent warehouse leaves the local variable NULL, so warehouse comparisons match no rows. Duplicate matching filter names are assigned without ordering.

Empty matching work produces an empty chart; outer SUM values for work units, instructions and condition counts can be NULL, while estimated-time ISNULL gives zero and the closed COUNT gives zero. COUNT(DISTINCT WORK_UNIT) excludes NULL work-unit values.

A work unit in two conditions contributes to both per-condition distinct counts; the summed unit total is not a warehouse-wide distinct count. A NULL group gets localized category text but NULL description.
output_shape: Seven result sets: chart rows with binding/category/data/description/axis/drilldown/title fields, followed by six one-row scalar result sets for units, instructions, estimated time, open, in-process and recently closed instructions.

ordered_branches.explanation: Parse filter text and assign warehouse.
Read nonclosed detail instructions in either source or destination warehouse; join work-group description, group by work group and description, count distinct work units, order by count descending.
Group nonclosed detail instructions by condition, sum per-condition distinct units and instruction counts, estimated time and open/in-process instruction counts.
Count closed detail instructions in WORK_INSTRUCTION_VIEW whose stamp is at or after UTC now minus one hour. Return the six scalars after the chart.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: No stored quantities or statuses are changed by this body.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: GENERIC_CONFIG_DETAIL descriptions and culture-dependent resources affect presentation. Its identifier join followed by a record-type WHERE condition can exclude work when only other record-type matches exist; duplicate descriptions can split chart groups.
error_and_return_handling: SET NOCOUNT ON/OFF; normal explicit RETURN 0 and a final @@ERROR/GOTO handler. This single late check is not comprehensive handling of every prior statement; errors can propagate before it.
contract.transaction_ownership: No explicit transaction, commit, rollback, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced by this body; caller/session semantics remain authoritative.
concurrency: Chart, totals and recent-closed count are separate queries without a common snapshot transaction in the body. Concurrent changes can make the result sets disagree even with identical filters.
contract.trigger_behavior: No persistent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE in this body; no DML trigger is activated by its reads.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: The SDK example is a binding pattern and differs from the captured deployment: the example has a chart only, while this body adds six scalar result sets and a detail-instruction predicate. Active screen bindings and exact completion-event timing are unverified.

limitations: This is the retained 2026-09-29 replica capture, not a new database inspection. The .sql file is the complete captured sys.sql_modules.definition encoded as UTF-8, including original comments, literals and line endings; nothing is prepended or reformatted. Captured definition text is not a complete deployment script: permissions, SET options, session context and dependencies are separate. No routine was executed. Static references do not establish branch execution, current use or runtime table scans. Vendor-base versus customer customization ownership is not established by names or comments.
A captured source reference establishes a static relationship, not that a module ran, a branch was reached, or a table is currently active.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.

DDL, DBCC, permission statements and metadata-function arguments are not comprehensively classified by the parser. Their table relationships depend on captured catalog dependencies or reviewed effects; unmatched identifiers/string arguments remain non-credit observations.
Identifier tokens and string-contained names are separate non-credit observations. Column names and configuration text can match table names; neither proves an executed table access.
Foreign keys are structural relationships and never count as procedure/function usage. View paths are catalog/source paths; attached trigger paths are possibilities, not proof the event fired.
Owner backup/leftover and item-master-failure suggestions are hypotheses. Name patterns and missing references do not validate them. No deletion recommendation is made.
Current replica status is owner-attested. This task documents the captured source as-is and requires no application version/build or extension development.
